summary: First iteration end-to-end testing of RestaurantOS SaaS. All 21 backend pytest tests pass (100%). All frontend flows render correctly for the seeded owner account. No critical blockers found. Only minor recharts width warning on dashboard load and a non-blocking CORS/cookie flag that may bite later.

minor.issue: Server sets httpOnly access_token cookie AND returns bearer token. get_current_user prefers cookie over Authorization header. If a frontend/browser session first registers (gets cookie) and later logs in as different user without clearing cookie, requests using Bearer of new user may silently resolve to old cookie-based user. Low risk in current frontend but worth noting.

allow_origins=['*'] with allow_credentials=False. Cookies therefore cannot be used cross-origin from browser fetches in production; frontend relies on Authorization header (works fine via /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js). Acceptable for current Bearer-based flow.

count_documents uses created_at >= 'YYYY-MM-DD' string compared to ISO datetime strings. Works because ISO dates sort lexicographically, but mixing string-prefix compare with ISO is fragile. Cosmetic.

issues: Recharts warns 'width(-1) and height(-1) of chart should be greater than 0' on first paint (ResponsiveContainer in hidden/0-sized parent). Charts still render correctly after layout settles, but consider setting explicit min-height on the chart card to remove the console warning.

action_items: (Optional) Add explicit min-height to dashboard/analytics chart containers to silence recharts width=-1 warnings
(Optional, hardening) In get_current_user, if Authorization header is present, prefer it over cookie — avoids stale cookie shadowing bearer token when multiple users share a browser session
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~930 lines; still manageable but close to the 700-line split threshold — consider splitting into routers/auth.py, routers/menu.py, routers/orders.py, routers/analytics.py for maintainability.
set_auth_cookie uses secure=False — fine for local dev but must be True in production (behind HTTPS).
allow_credentials=False with allow_origins='*' is the only safe combo right now; if cookie auth is later needed from browser, replace '*' with explicit FRONTEND_URL and flip credentials to True.
seed_demo is idempotent only on the admin user existence check — if admin exists but child collections were cleared, seed won't re-populate. Consider seeding each collection independently if empty.

_create_order recomputes totals server-side using price_map (good). However if an item_id is invalid, price_map.get returns 0 silently and the line is still added with price 0 — should reject order with 400 on unknown items.
Public POST /api/public/restaurant/{slug}/order has no rate limiting or captcha — potential abuse vector in production.

seed_data_creation: No new seed data created by test. Several TEST_ prefixed tenants created via /api/auth/register for isolation test — harmless, isolated in their own restaurant_id scope.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend regression suite is at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (21 tests, all green). Covers auth, categories, items, tables+QR, stock, orders lifecycle (pending→preparing→ready→served), analytics dashboard + trends, public menu, public order, and multi-tenant isolation. IMPORTANT: the seeded owner karim@restaurantos.dz cannot use shared requests.Session across tests because /auth/register and /auth/login both set an httpOnly cookie and the backend get_current_user prefers cookie over Authorization — use requests.Session per test or pop cookies. Frontend uses Bearer token in localStorage 'rx_token' via /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js so no browser-side cookie issues.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs blocking functionality were found. The only notable architectural quirk is the cookie-vs-bearer precedence in get_current_user; documented above as a minor hardening item.
